findings.current: If their medicine could’ve treated this, they would’ve done something long ago.
findings.defect: The draft makes the physicians responsible for failing to act, although the Emperor says he would have taken action; he has kept the illness from them.
findings.rationale: The following sentence explicitly says the Emperor hid his condition even from the imperial physicians.
findings.replacement: If their medicine could’ve treated this, I would’ve sought their help long ago.
findings.source: 그들의 의술로 치료할 수 있는 병이었다면 진즉 손을 썼을 거야.

findings.current: Thanks to the new scars that had finally made their faces distinguishable, I could tell them apart now.
findings.defect: Plural “scars” changes the single new scar used to distinguish the twins.
findings.rationale: The source specifies 흉터 in the singular as the distinguishing mark.
findings.replacement: A new scar finally let me tell their faces apart.
findings.source: 새로 생긴 흉터로 드디어 얼굴을 구분할 수 있게 된 쌍둥이 무장이 나를 기다리고 있었다.

findings.current: “Who knows? There’s no reason you need to know.”
findings.defect: “Who knows?” suggests the Emperor does not know the answer, rather than declining to tell Taekyung.
findings.rationale: 글쎄 is an evasive preface here; the Emperor subsequently gives the timing.
findings.replacement: “Well. I don’t see why you need to know.”
findings.source: “글쎄. 그걸 자네가 알아야 할 이유는 없지.”

findings.current: “Are you going to silence the witness?”
findings.defect: “Silence” leaves out the explicit threat of killing to keep the secret.
findings.rationale: 살인멸구 specifically means killing someone to prevent disclosure.
findings.replacement: “Are you going to kill me to keep me quiet?”

findings.current: “Not a chance. I’m going to live until I’m old enough to shit myself.”
findings.defect: The draft replaces the source’s image of smearing feces on a wall with incontinence, changing both the action and the joke.
findings.rationale: 벽에 똥칠할 때까지 uses the wall-smearing image to mean living to an extreme old age.
findings.replacement: “Not a chance. I’m going to live until I’m so old I’m smearing shit on the walls.”

findings.current: “After enduring more than ten winters, spring has finally come. That’s enough for me.”
findings.defect: The draft turns one figurative winter lasting over ten years into a count of separate winters.
findings.rationale: 십 년이 넘는 겨울 describes the duration of his ordeal as a long winter, contrasted with spring’s arrival.
findings.replacement: “After enduring a winter that lasted more than ten years, spring has finally come. That’s enough for me.”
findings.source: “십 년이 넘는 겨울을 버틴 끝에 바야흐로 봄이 찾아왔으니, 그것으로 되었다.”

findings.current: “Come on, why are you all making this so awkward?”
findings.defect: “Awkward” loses Taekyung’s bashful reaction to being honored.
findings.rationale: 낯간지럽게 conveys embarrassment at the flattering display, not discomfort with a social mistake.

findings.current: The Emperor, who’d been chuckling softly, suddenly broke into a coughing fit.
findings.defect: A coughing fit overstates the brief cough that precedes the blood.
findings.rationale: 잔기침 denotes a light cough; the ensuing blood is what makes the moment alarming.
findings.replacement: The Emperor, who’d been chuckling softly, suddenly gave a small cough.
findings.source: 작게 너털웃음을 흘리던 황제가 돌연 잔기침을 내뱉은 것은.

summary: The draft is largely faithful, but it changes who could have sought treatment, multiplies a distinguishing scar, and alters several meaningful lines of dialogue and imagery.
